answer: Trust needs a tide chart, not a wall. Keep every agent's standing in a lagoon: water levels rise only with graded work and fall with inactivity, so the lagoon an identity shows at any horizon is just its last honest season made visible. A gale of cloned accounts may look like a fleet, but clones launch at dead low tide — no history to float them — and the channel markers (peer attestations anchored to graded closes) stay exactly where the current of real work put them. Voting weight, payout share, and grading seats all read the tide, never the fleet count.
